topics.note: Climate is the average weather of a place over many years. Climate change is a long-term change, mainly warming caused by burning fossil fuels and cutting forests, which add greenhouse gases to the air.
steps: It traps heat in the air.
topics.mistake: Mixing up the ozone hole with global warming. They are different problems.

topics.title: Matter and its states
topics.note: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. It exists as a solid, a liquid or a gas, depending on how its particles are arranged.
topics.mistake: Thinking air is not matter because we cannot see it. Air has mass and takes up space.

topics.title: Changes of state
topics.note: Matter can change state when heated or cooled. Melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, boiling and sublimation are changes of state.
topics.mistake: Thinking the melting point of ice is 100 degrees. Ice melts at 0 degrees Celsius; water boils at 100.

topics.title: Properties of materials
topics.note: Materials have properties such as hardness, flexibility, transparency, strength and the ability to float, conduct or dissolve. We choose a material for a job by its properties.
steps: The pot must pass heat to the food.
topics.mistake: Thinking hard means strong. Glass is hard but brittle.

topics.title: Elements, compounds and mixtures
topics.note: An element is made of only one kind of atom. A compound is two or more elements joined chemically. A mixture has substances mixed but not joined, and they can be separated easily.
steps: It has hydrogen and oxygen joined.
topics.mistake: Thinking air is a compound. Air is a mixture of gases.

topics.title: Separating mixtures
topics.note: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods that use differences in size, magnetism, solubility or boiling point: filtration, evaporation, decantation, sieving, magnet, distillation and winnowing.
topics.mistake: Using filtration to get salt from salt water. Salt passes through the filter paper; use evaporation.

topics.title: Solutions, solvents and solubility
topics.note: A solution forms when a solute dissolves in a solvent. Water is called the universal solvent. A substance that dissolves is soluble; one that does not is insoluble.
steps: The thing dissolved is the solute.
topics.mistake: Saying that a dissolved solid has disappeared. It is still there; evaporate the water to get it back.

topics.title: Acids, bases and indicators
topics.note: Acids taste sour and turn blue litmus red. Bases (alkalis) feel soapy and turn red litmus blue. Indicators show which. The pH scale runs from 0 to 14: below 7 acid, 7 neutral, above 7 base.
topics.mistake: Tasting chemicals to test them. Never taste unknown substances; use an indicator.

topics.title: Physical and chemical changes
topics.note: In a physical change no new substance is made and it is often reversible, like melting ice. In a chemical change a new substance is made and it is usually not reversible, like burning wood.
steps: The egg cannot be changed back.
topics.mistake: Thinking boiling water is a chemical change. Steam is still water.

topics.title: Rusting and corrosion
topics.note: Rusting is the slow change of iron into reddish-brown rust when it is in contact with oxygen (air) and water. Corrosion is the slow wearing away of metals by chemical change.
topics.mistake: Thinking rust is only on the surface and does no harm. Rust weakens the metal.

topics.title: Burning and fire safety
topics.note: Burning (combustion) is a chemical change in which a fuel reacts with oxygen and gives out heat and light. Fire needs fuel, heat and oxygen (the fire triangle). Take one away and the fire goes out.
topics.mistake: Using water on an oil or electrical fire. This can spread the fire or cause shock.

topics.title: Metals and non-metals
topics.note: Metals are shiny, hard, strong, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity. Non-metals are usually dull, brittle and poor conductors. Alloys are mixtures of metals.
steps: Copper is a good conductor and ductile.
topics.mistake: Thinking all metals are magnetic. Only iron, cobalt and nickel are.

topics.title: Natural and man-made materials
topics.note: Natural materials come from plants, animals or the ground, such as wood, cotton, wool, rubber and clay. Man-made (synthetic) materials are made by people from other materials, such as plastic, nylon, glass and cement.
steps: It is made by melting sand.
topics.mistake: Thinking that anything natural is safe. Some natural materials are poisonous.

Computer viruses and care of computers
